entities.title: Java 21
entities.summary: From 0.3.0 the library needs Java 21; it was 17 up to 0.2.
entities.context: library-api §3 makes Outcome an exhaustive sum type that callers take apart by case.
entities.decision: pom.xml sets maven.compiler.release to 21. Outcome is a sealed interface with record cases, and TemporalValue, IntervalPoint and Bound are sealed too.
entities.rationale: Sealed interfaces, records and pattern switch let the compiler check that every outcome is handled.

entities.title: Years are BigInteger
entities.summary: Civil years are java.math.BigInteger in every typed value and in the JSON layer's arithmetic.
entities.context: Integers in UTV are decimal strings of any size (the arbitrary-precision obligation); library-api §1 names BigInteger for Java.
entities.decision: CivilDate and CivilYearMonth hold a BigInteger year; CivilDate.of and tryOf take a long or a BigInteger; Gregorian day arithmetic works on BigInteger. Instants and second amounts are exact rationals of BigIntegers.
entities.rationale: No year or fraction is ever rounded or wrapped; java.time's range is checked only when converting to it.

entities.title: The typed layer calls the JSON layer
entities.summary: Every typed operation builds UTV JSON, calls the 0.2 function and reads the answer back, through one bridge, Typed.
entities.context: library-api §2: every operation must agree with the JSON-level API and its fixtures, and implementations should call the 0.2 functions rather than re-implement them.
entities.decision: Typed.outcome, Typed.total and Typed.decode turn a UtvResult into an Outcome or a plain value. A total operation that answers anything but unique throws IllegalStateException, as a bug in the library.
entities.rationale: One implementation of each rule, tested by the shared fixtures, serves both layers.

entities.title: TemporalValue.parse, not Utv.parse
entities.summary: The contract's Utv.parse(text) is spelled TemporalValue.parse(text) in Java.
entities.context: Utv.parse(String json), JSON parsing with duplicate-key detection, has existed since 0.1 with the same signature.
entities.decision: Parsing any text-form value is TemporalValue.parse, a static method of the sealed interface; Utv.parse keeps its behaviour.
entities.rationale: The same name and signature cannot mean two things, and the 0.2 method stays.

entities.title: The method names the native intent
entities.summary: A java.time value with two readings is converted by the method that names the reading, so no intent-required outcome arises.
entities.context: everyday-api, Native interop: the caller names the intent, and a value tied to the host's local zone is refused.
entities.decision: Typed: FixedOffsetDateTime.from(OffsetDateTime) reads the wall time at its offset and Instant.from(OffsetDateTime) the instant. JSON layer: JavaTime.fromOffsetDateTime and fromDate take a JavaTime.As. java.util.Date is accepted only As.INSTANT; a civil reading is unsupported (local-zone). Conversions back return an Outcome (or NativeResult) with precision-loss or zone-dropped warnings, or unsupported (out-of-native-range).
entities.rationale: The target type is the intent, so nothing is chosen silently, and Date's fields come from ZoneId.systemDefault().

entities.title: toZonedDateTime checks the JDK's tz database
entities.summary: Converting a zoned value to java.time.ZonedDateTime is the one place the library reads the JDK's tz database.
entities.context: The library never reads the host's tz database, but a ZonedDateTime cannot exist without one.
entities.decision: ZonedIntent.toZonedDateTime and JavaTime.toZonedDateTime need an asserted offset (from resolve or Instant.inZone) and check it with ZonedDateTime.ofStrict: invalid (offset-mismatch) if the JDK disagrees, unsupported (unknown-zone) if it lacks the zone. Without an asserted offset the value is refused, because choosing an offset is resolve's job.
entities.rationale: The JDK's rules are used only to build the native value, never to choose an answer.
